The second pathway shows Ent-Gloeosteretriol targeting Serine/threonine-protein kinase ICK, which is a target of Oblonganoside C, another compound with potential anti-leukemic activity. Both pathways ultimately lead to the inhibition of leukemia cells, indicating that Ent-Gloeosteretriol may act through distinct but related mechanisms to modulate cellular processes in leukemia. The evidence is consistent across two independent scoring systems, suggesting a plausible biological relationship. However, the exact nature of the interaction and the precise mechanisms by which Ent-Gloeosteretriol influences leukemia cell behavior remain to be fully elucidated.
